# Installation {.unnumbered}

## Quarto

To check whether Quarto is already installed, run:

```bash
quarto -v
```

If you see `command not found`, follow the [official Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) to install it. Once installed, the same command should return the version number:

::: {data-code-copy="false"}
```bash
user@office:~$ quarto -v
1.10.18
```
:::

## Python and Jupyter

Quarto uses Jupyter to execute Python code blocks and capture their output. Create a virtual environment and install Jupyter into it:

```bash
python3 -m venv myenv
source myenv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install jupyter
```

:::{.callout-note collapse="true" title="Windows users"}
Activate the virtual environment in PowerShell with:
```powershell
myenv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```
or in Command Prompt with:
```cmd
myenv\Scripts\activate.bat
```
Then install Jupyter the same way: `python3 -m pip install jupyter`
:::

# Writing your first document

Create a new file with the extension `.qmd`, for example `my_notes.qmd`, and add the following content:

```markdown
# My First Quarto Document
This is a simple Quarto document
```

Preview it in your browser by running:

```bash
quarto preview my_notes.qmd
```

This opens a live-reloading preview in your default browser.

## Adding Python code

To include executable Python code, use a `{python}` code block:

````markdown
# My First Quarto Document
This is a simple Quarto document

```{{python}}
print(3+3)
```
````

Save the file — the preview will refresh automatically and display the output below the code block.
